The ending feels natural, earned, and purposeful rather than abrupt or arbitrary. Throughout the story, the central conflict is the quiet, ambiguous, and noncommittal nature of Mara and Julian’s temporary relationship as the residency comes to an end. The story builds toward the quiet realization that their connection will neither blossom into a dramatic beginning nor receive the "dignity of an ending." The final image—a single, ordinary grain of sand falling from the pocket of her dress (a callback to a moment on the beach) that she places on the windowsill—perfectly encapsulates the themes of the story, offering thematic closure and a resonant resolution to their brief, understated intimacy.
